answer.answer: Little Cloud is a modest fight, but your inventory is the real risk. If storage is reasonably close, bank excess ammunition and consumables before continuing. Otherwise advance methodically and treat the tagged Regeneration Chamber only as reduced travel risk—not guaranteed recovery or replacement gear. Starry Night is easier: clear any roamers, open the final chest first, then loot the debris.

claims.value: Little Cloud is about 2/5 difficulty. Within 250 units it has 13 persistent hostile spawn entries: 8 tier-1 melee, 4 tier-1 ranged, and 1 tier-1 exploder, with no mapped Goliaths, Flingers, tier-2 enemies, or raid-class concentration. These markers represent possible persistent population, not 13 simultaneous attackers; the player later completed it and reported it was “no big deal.”

Protect the valuable load by banking excess ammunition and consumables first if storage is reasonably quick. If not, proceed methodically using the nearby respawn only to reduce travel risk. Keep replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding supplies in a separate safe recovery cache rather than inside the contested site.

A tagged or claimed Regeneration Chamber is not a complete recovery guarantee: direct field observation showed that a nearby claimed base could respawn the player yet provide no spare weapons or replacement materials, while corruption later disabled a contested base and its claimed Chamber, sending the player to the starting launcher. This comes from one encounter; the exact corruption threshold and general Chamber-disable rule remain unverified.

Starry Night is about 1/5 difficulty, with zero persistent hostile spawn markers within 250 units, although roaming enemies can still wander in. Its guaranteed final chest contains the Electronics Blueprint, Rotor Blueprint, 15 Armory Tokens, and a Frame Memory Module; clear wanderers and open that chest before looting debris.

answer.answer: The first Geo Scanner experience is now captured as durable operational guidance, with direct observation separated from unverified general mechanics and the loot ambiguity preserved.

claims.value: The first Geo Scanner required two deaths before success. After the first death, the player respawned at a nearby claimed base, but it had no spare weapons or replacement materials, forcing a walk back to Landerworks. On the next attempt, the scanner fire base had installed but unpowered turrets, so they provided no defense; after the player was overwhelmed, corruption disabled the contested base and its claimed Regeneration Chamber, and the player respawned at the starting launcher instead of locally.

The successful intervention was a fully built-out temporary fire base with every turret powered. With the automated defenses operating, the player completed the scanner and described the turrets continuously engaging—or “singing” against—the enemy as a strongly positive payoff.

The failure chain is direct player field evidence from one Geo Scanner encounter: corruption disabled that contested base and its claimed Regeneration Chamber. It does not establish an exact corruption threshold or a universal Regeneration Chamber disable rule; both remain unverified. Operationally, the observed possibility should be treated as a conservative failure condition, not promoted into a universal mechanic.

For future first-time scanner activations, treat the scanner as a deliberate defense event: claim a nearby Regeneration Chamber but assume the local checkpoint can fail; power every turret and verify that each tracks or fires before activation; keep a replacement weapon kit, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials in a separate safe cache outside the contested base’s likely corruption or failure area; and preserve a route to a stable production base or launcher as the final fallback. The completed scanner appeared to yield two particularly good food-related rewards or stacks, possibly involving a quantity of 20, but the dictated report is ambiguous. The scanner identity, exact item names, and exact counts remain unresolved and must not be normalized into facts.

answer.answer: Watch Session remains an evidence-bounded native-iPhone MVP: a five-state, across-the-room monitor whose hero countdown targets the next meaningful event. Opportunity guidance is separately versioned and provenance-labeled, while alerts and native behavior remain explicit, accessible, and conservative about what iOS can guarantee.

claims.value: The design is pinned to Early Access Update 1 through Hotfix 0.2.8, Steam build 23761620, released 2026-06-17, with structured source SRDB 2.3.4 captured 2026-07-11. Its cycle model is 54 minutes from local fire-wave impact to the next local impact. Creepy Jar has not published an official numerical phase formula; the model is strongly corroborated by starrupture.tools and an independent runtime-reading mod, so it must remain a versioned community/game-data model. Manual synchronization starts at 0:00 when the fire wall reaches the player. Confidence states are Unsynced, Manual sync - predicted, Confirmed at one later transition, Drift suspected, and Cycle data changed - re-sync required. Do not invent numerical accuracy; downgrade confidence after a large correction, device-clock or model-version change, uncertain pause, save/reload, or server stop. Until live Hotfix 0.2.8 validation covers several solo, hosted-co-op, and dedicated-server cycles, use predicted, expected, favorable, and lower threat—not exact, safe, or guaranteed.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Preserve the 54-minute engine model but present five player-facing states: Fire wave 0:00-0:30 (Remain sheltered), Cooling 0:30-1:30 (Remain sheltered), Recovery / quiet window 1:30-11:30 (Lower ambient threat; use the window), World active 11:30-51:30, about 40:00 (Ordinary enemies and ecology active), and Ruptura warning 51:30-54:00, about 2:30 (Return, bank loot, and shelter). The final warning’s internal boundaries still need live Hotfix 0.2.8 validation. The portrait screen keeps five layers visible without scrolling: sync/capability and degraded state; semantic hero state with a huge monospaced countdown and explicit target; threat instruction plus one action sentence; no more than two opportunity cards; then exact-time next events with only Mute one cycle and Re-sync always visible. The hero targets the next meaningful event: ordinary Vermin’s expected return during recovery, otherwise the next Ruptura or warning start. Retain one proportional whole-cycle rail for orientation, but add minimum-width labeled steps or a next-event list so the 30-second Fire wave and 60-second Cooling phase never collapse into unusable slivers. Color is atmospheric only and must be accompanied by text, symbols, and border treatment.

claims.value: Opportunities are separately versioned evidence records, not implied phase mechanics. Each OpportunityWindow stores an ID, start event or offset, end event or offset, action and caveat, evidence class and confidence, applicable game build, and applicable source snapshot. Initial guidance includes: reduced ordinary POI population during Recovery with triggered encounters possibly persisting; Oxallop during early recovery while lakebeds are dry; caves, Quartz, and Glowcaps during Recovery without guaranteed respawn; Ignitium immediately after Cooling through Recovery with variable spawn rate; experimental Star Tears timing in late recovery; variable Coralion/Vulpir egg opportunities after the wave; surface foliage and water described only as regrowth underway; and Sulheart hidden until exact current timing is validated. The Ignitium/Star Tears tradeoff should explicitly tell players that prioritizing Star Tears may mean leaving cooled Ignitium unharvested. claims.value: Enemy return and Ruptura require distinct sounds and haptic signatures, with text, symbols, borders, and optional patterns so neither color nor audio stands alone. The proposed enemy-return ladder is: 5 minutes, amber edge plus Finish or leave hard POIs, short double haptic and optional tone, normal notification; 2 minutes, persistent retreat banner, double tone/haptic, optional notification; 1 minute, red instruction and emphasized seconds, stronger cue, background notification off by default; 15 seconds, static danger border and large seconds, one final cue with no ticking; event, ORDINARY VERMIN RETURNING, urgent triple cue, notification or explicitly armed alarm. Pre-Ruptura cues are optional 10 minutes, then 5 minutes, 2:30, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact; an exit buffer may generate TURN BACK NOW earlier. Profiles are Full, Haptic only, and Visual only, with separate phase, enemy, Ruptura, and opportunity toggles, Mute one cycle, and preview; after resume, collapse missed cues to the strongest current-state message and never replay a backlog. On iOS, disable the idle timer only while the monitor scene is active and restore it afterward; offer dim OLED mode and never use background audio as a keep-alive. Schedule local notifications at absolute dates and reschedule after anchor, model, or policy changes; recompute from (now - anchor) modulo cycle duration on resume and deduplicate by cycle number plus event ID. Use one Live Activity for the currently armed event, not an indefinite self-advancing promise. AlarmKit may break through Silent mode and Focus, but requires authorization and must be created only after the player explicitly arms the next event or Watch Session—never as an endless automatic 54-minute alarm. Earlier iOS versions use normal notifications; Time Sensitive is separate opt-in, and Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Keep Re-sync, Mute one cycle, capability state, and Next alert at [local time] visible; support Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, and Reduce Motion; avoid flashing red, default per-second ticking, and per-second VoiceOver announcements.
